findings.description: DEFECT: all 23 frame-0 dots are one drawn cell downstream of the actual origin (route index 1 instead of 0). For example intake control plane origin (16,19) versus dot (16,20); ops queue first origin (25,10) versus dot (25,11); boot response origin (32,40) versus dot (31,40). The constant-mode origin rule applies too. Static stems/heads are present, but the rubric explicitly treats offset dot starts as direction unproven. The checks' origins:N/N assertions are contradicted by captured coordinates. This also fails animation.

DEFECT: seven routes visibly overwrite a corner with their dot, totaling 40 route-frame occupancies: q→reg at (10,12), reg→prov at (8,20), prov→mch at (9,28), mch→S3 at (11,35), mch→agent at (11,11), agent→public gRPC at (12,19), and webapi→Slack at (67,38). See unchanged blind record for every frame number. First-corner skipping is not an effective no-corner guarantee.

DEFECT: 14 routes skip a visible centerline cell at a corner, producing a two-cell move in a 200ms interval while other routes move one. In ops, frames 0→2 move q→SSH (25,11)→(25,12), one cell, while SSH→machines moves (2,29)→(3,30), two centerline cells. In provision, q→registry moves (13,11)→(12,12), two cells, while the boot-response dot moves (31,40)→(30,40), one. This is unequal visible-grid advance, not an objection to legal unequal arrival times. Odd frames repeat the preceding even frame; quantization itself is not failed.

The generator recorded the warnings and spent three candidates, but exhaustion of an attempt budget is not proof that no unambiguous placement exists; the exception is not established.

DEFECT: avoidable bridge at (37,38), the only crossing. The source does not constrain individual Postgres input-port order. Current fixed-port long queue route is reported forced, so length alone is not failed.
